label: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer

patch.objective: Choosing a deployment strategy -- canary, blue/green, rolling, traffic splitting, feature flags -- and defining success metrics from application or ML pipeline telemetry

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer exam guide (new version, live November 23): foundational infrastructure and governance ~18%, CI/CD pipelines ~30%, SRE practices ~18%, observability and troubleshooting ~22%, performance and cost optimization ~12%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the PDF on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 2.2 'Deployment strategies (e.g., canary, blue/green, rolling, traffic splitting, feature flags)' 'and defining success metrics based on application or ML pipeline telemetry'; 5.2 'Optimizing resource usage for cost and efficiency'. sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud Run: Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration (last updated 2026-11-10)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Relevant text: roll back with 'gcloud run services update-traffic SERVICE --to-revisions REVISION=100'; 'Rolling back traffic to a revision updates the routing configuration immediately'; deploy with 'gcloud run deploy --image IMAGE --no-traffic' then shift traffic in steps, for example 5 percent; '--no-traffic --tag TAG_NAME' lets you 'directly test the new revision at a specific URL, without serving traffic'; 'the percentages must add up to 100'; 'traffic routing adjustments are not instantaneous'.
